punchline: An average life is just four thousand weeks long.
thirty_sec: Journalist Oliver Burkeman wrote a productivity column for years and tested every system on himself, until one uncomfortable calculation stopped him: the average human life lasts roughly four thousand weeks. The book landed as a brake in the middle of hustle culture, reminding millions of readers that the real question of time management is not how to fit everything in, but what to leave out on purpose.
question: What will you say a clear, deliberate no to this week?
key_contrast: Getting faster is not the same as getting less busy.
